Another New York Story: Know Your Dealer or Know Your Lawyer’s Number

From A Reader:

I am familiar with what the senior in NY described.

See
"Let me tell you why we should settle only for legalization, and not decriminalization."
A Reader In New York Makes A Valuable Point, Learned The Hard Way.

I was walking with a friend on 6th Avenue in New York in the fall of 1998 when a man asked my friend if he wanted to buy some "weed". My friend walked off with the man. I didn’t see him until the next day!

Apparently, Giuliani hasn’t been satisfied with just placing cameras in the parks - he is sending police officers out on the streets and parading them as drug dealers.

My friend purchased $10 worth of marijuana - which, in New York, is very little, and was handcuffed by four police officers immediately, placed in a van, and driven around the city for hours until he spent the night in prison.

To me, this deceptive facade is quite a bit more scary than a person possessing a small amount of marijuana.

(Marijuananews note: Never buy marijuana from strangers. They could turn out to be narcs or some other sort of dangerous criminals.)
